candidates.text:
STOP TRYING TO “FIND YOURSELF.”

One of the strangest ideas modern people have swallowed is that somewhere deep inside them exists a pristine, finished, AUTHENTIC personality…

And your job is to go digging around until you “discover who you really are.”

Why?

What makes you think the current contents of your personality are sacred?

Half of what you call “me” is shit you accidentally picked up.

Your sense of humour.
Your relationship with money.
Your confidence.
Your taste.
Your posture.
Your standards.
The way you speak.
The things you are afraid of.
The amount of disrespect you tolerate.
What you believe you are capable of.
Where did all of that come from?
You think you consciously selected it??
LOL.
A gigantic percentage of your “identity” is simply the accumulated result of family, teachers, friends, girlfriends, embarrassing experiences at 14, random praise, random rejection, movies, music, algorithms, people you admired, people you hated, and whatever happened to be repeatedly placed in front of your nervous system.
And then at 25 you point at the finished pile and say:
“This is just who I am.”
NO.
That is who you have been CONDITIONED to be.
Important distinction.

Because once you understand that personality is far more plastic than people pretend, the entire project changes.

Stop asking:

“Who am I?”

Start asking:

“WHO AM I BECOMING?”

And better:

“Who have I consciously DECIDED to become?”

If you admire somebody’s vocabulary, steal the standard and train yours.

If you admire somebody’s composure, study it.

If you admire somebody’s courage, deliberately place yourself in situations that demand courage until courage becomes normal.

If you speak like shit, improve your speech.

If you dress like shit, develop taste.

If you’re socially timid, train social boldness.

If your standards are low, raise them and tolerate the discomfort of no longer fitting neatly into your old environment.

This applies to almost everything.

People have this ridiculous reverence for their existing limitations.

“I’m just introverted.”
“I’ve never been disciplined.”
“I’m not really a reader.”
“I’m bad with money.”
“I’ve always been anxious.”
“I’m just not that type of person.”

Okay?

And?

Since WHEN did your past get voting rights over your future?

Your previous behaviour is evidence of your previous conditioning.

That’s all.

You can condition something else.

This is why I have always found the obsession with “authenticity” slightly suspicious.

Authentic to WHAT?

The version of you created by your parents?
Your secondary school?
Your ex?
Your hometown?
Your Twitter feed?
Fuck that.
There is enormous power in becoming ARTIFICIAL on purpose long enough that the artificial becomes natural.
At first, the new behaviour feels fake.
GOOD.
Of course it does.

Anything outside your existing identity feels fake because your nervous system has not normalised it yet.

Repeat it.

Reinforce it.

Build evidence.

Eventually what required conscious effort becomes automatic.

Then one day somebody who knew you five years ago meets you again and says:

“Wow. You’ve changed.”

Correct.

That was the fucking point.
You are not an archaeological site.
You are an ENGINEERING PROJECT.
BUILD YOURSELF.
